title: The 13-14-15 Triangle
statement: A triangle has sides $13$, $14$ and $15$. Find the radius of its inscribed circle.
hints: Heron's formula, or drop the altitude to the side of length $14$.
solution: The semiperimeter is $s = 21$ and Heron gives area $\sqrt{21\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6} = 84$. Then $r = 84/21 = 4$.

solution_figures.alt: Triangle ABC with AB = 13, BC = 14 and CA = 15, and its inscribed circle with centre I. The radius r from I meets BC at right angles at the touch point D. Segments from I to the three vertices split the triangle into three smaller triangles whose heights are all r.
